title: Evaluating LLM Outputs: Golden Sets, EM, F1 & ROUGE-L
summary: You can't improve an LLM feature you can't measure. Learn how to build a golden set, score answers with SQuAD-style exact match and token F1 or with ROUGE-L, attach a bootstrap confidence interval, and catch per-example regressions before you ship a new model or prompt.
takeaways: A golden set (fixed inputs with trusted reference answers) turns 'it seems better' into a number you can track across releases.
Normalize before you compare. Lowercasing and stripping punctuation and articles stop formatting noise from counting as errors.
EM is strict, token F1 gives partial credit by multiset overlap, and ROUGE-L rewards words in the right order via the longest common subsequence.
A mean score on 200 examples has an error bar. Report a bootstrap CI and look at which examples regressed, not just the average.

steps.label: Curate the golden set
steps.detail: Representative inputs with one or more human-approved reference answers, versioned like code.

steps.label: Generate
steps.detail: Run the baseline and the candidate (new model, prompt or retriever) on every input.

steps.label: Normalize + score
steps.detail: Per example: exact match and token F1 for short answers, ROUGE-L for longer ones. Take the max over references.

steps.label: Aggregate with uncertainty
steps.detail: Average the scores and bootstrap a confidence interval with a fixed seed.

steps.label: Diff the runs
steps.detail: List per-example regressions and improvements, and gate the release on the overall delta.

terms.definition: A fixed, versioned evaluation dataset of inputs with trusted reference outputs, used to compare model versions.
1 if the normalized prediction equals a normalized reference answer, else 0.
Harmonic mean of token precision and recall, computed on the multiset overlap of prediction and reference tokens.
Precision, recall and F computed from the longest common subsequence of candidate and reference words.
The longest sequence of tokens that appears in both texts in the same order, not necessarily contiguously.
A confidence interval from resampling the examples with replacement and taking percentiles of the recomputed mean.
